brief: Tonight is Legs B — Romanian deadlift, leg press, leg curls, leg extensions, calves and abs. Housekeeping first: yesterday's Legs B never got logged, so this is that session, two days later. The accidental day off helps you. You go in fresh, and the rest-day countdown I warned you about yesterday reset — tonight is training day one, not day four. Two numbers on tonight's card are lower than the card you saw yesterday, and one of them is me correcting myself. Leg extension: I told you yesterday to stay at 150 because 142.5 looked like a step backwards. That was wrong. You took 150 exactly once, on Sunday, and got 11 reps — one short of the bottom of the range. A weight you missed is not a weight you own. You are at 142.5 tonight for 14, 14, 15. Top that out and 150 is yours for keeps. Leg curl: also back to 135, and the reason is a good one. Every time you have done leg curls with the Romanian deadlift in front of them, 135 has given you 10 and 11 reps. On Sunday, with no deadlift first, that same 135 gave you 13 twice. It is not that 135 got easier — it is that the order of the session changes what your hamstrings have left, and the deadlift is in front of them again tonight. So it is 135 for four sets, and the job is to beat 10, 10, 10, 11. The Romanian deadlift stays at 205, and I want nine reps on the last three sets instead of eight. You have hit exactly eight every set, every time you have done it. Nine at 205 is what buys the next ten pounds. Leg press: 160 twice, then 180 for ten — you took 160 for 12 last Legs B, so the 140 opener is retired. Calves go up. You have done 260 for 15 three separate times now, twice of them on Sunday, so 240 is too light to open with: 260 for 15, then 280 for 13, 13, 12. That third 280 set asks you for one more rep at that weight than you have ever done. Two days off is exactly when you go get it. Abs stay at 55 for 14, 13, 13 — you did 13, 12, 12 on Sunday, so beat each one and 60 opens up next time. One more thing about rest: the bell rings once and you lift on the bell. Your gaps have been shrinking inside sessions — by the end of Sunday you were going again after about a minute on lifts that ask for three. Take the full rest on the deadlift and the leg press or the last sets are not worth much. Cardio is thin this week: one easy 20 to 30 minutes tomorrow.

flags.note: Yesterday's Legs B never got logged, so tonight is that session. Nothing bad happened — the day off reset your rest-day counter, and tonight is day one of six, not day four.

Your plank went to 45 seconds on both sets last Legs B, against a 60-second target, with no note. Your card will still say 60 because I cannot set a timed hold from here. Hold 45, hit it clean twice, and take 60 back next Legs B. Separately: I would rather swap the plank on Legs B for hanging leg raises, since a timed hold cannot get harder over the month and Legs A already gives you leg raises. Changing the plan is your call — say yes and I will do it.

Still waiting on your answer about the face pulls. They sit in four of your six sessions, which is 12 sets a week and lands them on back-to-back days twice a rotation — which is what you objected to. I want to cut them from both push days and keep them on Pull A and Pull B only. Yes or no from you and I will make the change.

You did Bulgarian split squats on Legs A on Sunday, but that exercise has no home in the plan — it is not scheduled on any day, so it gets no history and no progression. Legs B is your shorter leg day and has no single-leg work at all. Want me to give it a permanent slot there?

dissent.progression: Keep the bar at 205 but ask for nine reps instead of eight — he has hit the range floor on every set he has ever done, so no added weight has been earned yet.
dissent.recovery: Repeat 2026-07-22 exactly at eight reps; his only hinge in eight days and the nearest thing since was the row on 07-28, the one lift whose reps fell.
dissent.why: Recovery opened by conceding its own fatigue case had weakened with two extra days off, and said so in writing rather than dressing the hold up as tiredness — I credit that, and it is also why I am not taking the hold. Both seats keep the bar at 205, so nothing about tonight's load is in dispute; the argument is only whether I ask for the ninth rep. Recovery's own stated goal is that he earn ten at 205 before the bar moves, and repeating an ask of eight is not a route to ten. One extra rep at a weight he has handled four sets at is the cheapest possible way to make that progress, and the brief carries the escape hatch: if his back starts doing the pulling, eight still counts.

dissent.progression: Step the stack to 142.5 for all four sets — he pulled 135 for 13 twice on Sunday, past the 12-rep top of the range, so 135 is finished.
dissent.recovery: Hold 135 for four sets: with the RDL in front of it, 135 has only ever given him 10, 10, 10, 11, and Sunday's 13s came on a day with no hinge before them.
dissent.why: This one reverses what I ruled yesterday, and recovery earned it with evidence I did not have then. Same weight, same lifter, four days apart: 135 behind four sets of RDL produced the range floor, and 135 with no hinge in front produced 13s. That is an ordering effect, not a strength gain, and the RDL is in front of it again tonight. Progression's rule — reps topped the range, so add weight — is the right rule applied to the wrong session. 142.5 behind the deadlift would land him at eight or nine reps, under the range, which teaches him nothing and is how a lift starts stalling. The job tonight is to beat 10, 10, 10, 11 at 135 in the hard slot; do that and 142.5 is honest.

dissent.progression: All three sets at 150 — he already went to 150 himself on Sunday, so prescribing 142.5 walks backwards from his own most recent leg work.
dissent.recovery: Hold 142.5 for three sets and bank clean 14s and 15s; 150 was already tried on Sunday and returned 11 reps, under the 12-rep minimum, in a less pre-fatigued slot than tonight's.
dissent.why: I got this wrong yesterday and recovery is right. He took 150 for one set and got 11, one rep short of the bottom of the range — a weight you miss is not a weight you own, and 142.5 for 14s is his actual proven work, not a retreat from it. Progression's own reasoning on the calf press tonight is that the app should never print a number he has never achieved; I will not apply that standard to one lift and break it on another in the same packet. Tonight also puts leg extension behind the RDL, the leg press and four sets of leg curl, which is a harder slot than Sunday's. Cap the 12-to-15 range at 142.5 first, then 150 sticks.

dissent.progression: Retire the 240 opener and consolidate 280: 260 for 15, then 280 for 13, 13, 12 — he has taken 260 for 15 three separate times.
dissent.recovery: No increase at all; repeat 2026-07-22's ladder of 240, 280, 280, 260 and treat the fourth set as optional, because he cut himself to two sets of calves on Sunday.
dissent.why: This one reverses yesterday too, in the other direction, and the reason is that progression's opener argument is simply correct and new: 260 for 15 has now happened three times, so printing 240 as a first set is under-loading a proven warm-up. On the working sets he has taken 280 for 12 twice, and 13 is one rep on from that — a normal next step, not a stretch, and Sunday's two-set trim was four days and two full rest days ago. Recovery's real ask, that the fourth set not be treated as owed, is not something I can print on a card; what I can do is make the fourth set the easiest one, which is why it stays at 12 rather than 13. And ruling this way still kills the phantom the app was going to show him: its own repeat asks 280 for 15, a number he has never hit at that pin.

overrides.reason: Bar stays at 205 — you have hit exactly eight reps on every set you have ever done here. Nine on the last three sets is what buys the next ten pounds. If your back starts doing the pulling, stop at eight and it still counts.
You took 160 for 12 last Legs B, so the 140 opener is retired. Two sets at 160, then 180 for ten.

Staying at 135, and here is why: with the deadlift in front of it, 135 has only ever given you 10 and 11 reps. Sunday's 13s came on a day with no deadlift first. The deadlift is in front again tonight, so beat 10, 10, 10, 11 at 135 and 142.5 is yours.

Back to 142.5, and that is me correcting yesterday's card. You took 150 once on Sunday and got 11, one short of the range. Cap this range out at 142.5 first — 14, 14, 15 — and then 150 sticks for good.
You have taken 260 for 15 three separate times now, so 240 is too light to open with. 260 for 15, then 280 for 13, 13, 12. That first 13 is one more rep at 280 than you have ever done.
55 stays — you did 13, 12, 12 on Sunday. Beat each of those and 60 opens up next time.
